title: Roguelette: using AI assistance to build and verify a roulette roguelike in Unity
author: Particular-Sugar-143
selftext:
I’m the solo developer of Roguelette, a PC roulette roguelike made in Unity with AI assistance in coding and some visual assets. You choose three bets, keep useful results and reroll the other balls to beat a round target. Tricks and charms change the possibilities across a run.



One practical lesson from working with AI has been to verify the gameplay it helps implement, especially the score preview and held-ball behaviour. For this clip, a recording tool calls the normal game actions, uses reproducible random seeds and checks that the rolled numbers and final score match the real game calculation. It never assigns a result or score. The first roll gives 2 points against a target of 10; holding the 17 and rerolling the two misses produces 2 × 5 × 5 = 50.



This is current gameplay, not an AI-generated video. There is no public demo yet. I’m sharing both the game and that verification approach here; the AI-assisted visual assets are also disclosed on Steam.
